# inkmap

Per-pixel foreground coverage for photographed marks.

Given a photo of a printed mark and a **model** of its shape, say — for every pixel —
how much of it is foreground (the mark) and how much is background (the substrate). Not
a boolean mask: a continuous 0–1 area fraction, accurate enough to measure on.

```bash
pip install inkmap
```

```python
import inkmap

coverage = inkmap.foreground("photo.jpg")   # (H, W) float32 in [0, 1]
```

## The idea

Decoding a QR code is a solved problem. Reading text is a solved problem. **Measuring**
the mark itself is not: if you need to know the reflectance, density, or colour of the
printed material — as opposed to what it says — you need to know exactly which pixels
are mark, which are substrate, and which are neither.

The shape is the input, not a special case. A model answers one question — *is this
point, in my own coordinate system, foreground?* — and everything else (locating,
sub-pixel refinement, rasterising, measuring) is written against that one question. So
QR symbols, barcodes, printed letters and arbitrary artwork all go through one pipeline.

```python
from inkmap import models

inkmap.find(photo)                                        # auto-detect QR / barcode
inkmap.find(photo, model=models.text_model("ABC"), quad=q)  # printed text
inkmap.find(photo, model=models.RasterModel(logo), quad=q)  # anything you can draw
inkmap.find(photo, model=models.PolygonModel(outlines), quad=q)   # exact vector shape
```

Writing your own is two members and no base class:

```python
class Disc:
    extent = (20.0, 20.0)      # model space is 20 x 20 units
    feature_size = 10.0        # smallest feature that must be resolved

    def occupancy(self, u, v):                    # vectorised
        return (u - 10) ** 2 + (v - 10) ** 2 < 81

inkmap.find(photo, model=Disc(), quad=corners)
```

## What you get back

```python
ink = inkmap.find("photo.jpg")        # an InkMap, or None

ink.placement.quad                    # (4, 2) corners — a quadrilateral, not a
                                      # rectangle; perspective is expected
ink.placement.transform               # (3, 3) model space -> image pixels
ink.placement.pixels_per_feature      # the resolution figure that governs everything

ink.coverage                          # (H, W) float32 — foreground area fraction
ink.region                            # OUTSIDE / MARGIN / BACKGROUND / FOREGROUND
ink.weight                            # (H, W) float32 — safe-to-measure weighting
```

Then measure:

```python
result = inkmap.measure("photo.jpg", ink)

result.foreground_mean                # sRGB-linearised mean over safe pixels
result.background_mean
result.contrast
result.measurability.ok               # False if this image can't support it
```

`measure` accepts any frame registered to the one you located in, so geometry can be
established once on the sharpest image and reused across exposures, channels or
modalities.

## The three 0–1 channels

Conflating these is the fastest route to a wrong measurement:

|              | what it is                                                           | use it for                                          |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `coverage`   | **geometric** — fraction of the pixel’s area under foreground        | reporting, print QC, finding mixed pixels           |
| `weight`     | **blur-aware** — coverage eroded by how far the PSF actually reaches | **the only channel that should gate a measurement** |
| `confidence` | **epistemic** — how much to trust the label here                     | quality gating, artefact rejection                  |

If the underlying reality is binary, “probability this pixel is foreground” is
`confidence`. If it isn’t — a pixel genuinely straddling an edge — the degree of
membership is `coverage`. They are different numbers and both are worth having.

Measured on synthetic scenes with exact ground truth, recovering a foreground-only
signal at 6 px per feature:

| pixel selection                               | no blur   | σ=1       | σ=2       | σ=3       |
|-----------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| `coverage > 0.5` (what a threshold gives you) | −3.3%     | −12.2%    | −23.3%    | −32.4%    |
| `coverage == 1.0` (geometrically pure)        | −0.0%     | −8.0%     | −19.9%    | −30.1%    |
| **`weight`** (PSF-eroded)                     | **+0.0%** | **−0.2%** | **−0.6%** | **−1.5%** |

Geometric purity is *not* sufficient: blur drags background signal into pixels entirely
under foreground, and that contamination has a different footprint from partial
coverage — so no coverage-based weighting removes it. Only spatial erosion does. See
[docs/validation.md]().

## Terminology

The classes are **foreground** and **background**, never dark/light — appearance
inverts (white-on-black print, reflectance-reversed symbols, inverted imaging), so an
appearance-based name would mean the mark in one image and the substrate in the next.
`Polarity` carries that mapping explicitly:

```python
from inkmap import Polarity
inkmap.find(photo, polarity=Polarity.FOREGROUND_IS_LIGHT)
```

The continuous value is **coverage**, after ISO 12647-2 *area coverage*. Full
cross-field mapping to ISO/IEC 18004, 15415, DIBCO, printing, matting, remote sensing
and medical-imaging vocabulary: [docs/terminology.md]().

## How it works

```default
photograph ──► locate ──► recover model ──► refine transform ──► rasterise ──► erode
```

1. **Locate** — a cascade of `zxing-cpp`, OpenCV’s Aruco-based QR detector and OpenCV’s
   classic detector, plus linear barcodes. On 189 real photographs: zxing 74%, aruco
   68%, OpenCV 43%, **union 80%**. For marks nothing can auto-detect, `inkmap.place()`
   takes the corners from you.
2. **Recover the model** — from a bit-exact rectification where a decoder offers one,
   otherwise sampled from the image. *Never* by re-encoding a decoded payload:
   error-correction level, mask pattern and code-set choices are not recoverable from
   the text, so re-encoding can silently produce a different pattern.
3. **Refine** — align the rendered model to the photograph with ECC. Four locator
   corners are four observations; the model has thousands. Takes corner error from
   ~1 px to **0.02–0.03 px** (4–53× depending on conditions).
4. **Rasterise** — supersample each pixel, back-project through the transform, ask the
   model `occupancy(u, v)`. Exact up to the supersampling rate, and independent of
   lighting. Coverage MAE against exact ground truth is **0.0000–0.0005**.
5. **Erode to a weight** — by ~2× the estimated blur σ, because geometric purity is not
   enough (see the table above).

Decoding is optional throughout. A mark whose material barely deposited will not
decode, and that is exactly the case that must still work.

Sub-pixel geometry turns out to hinge on **three half-pixel conventions agreeing** —
pixel-centre vs pixel-corner rasterisation, the template raster, and the fact that
different locators disagree about what a “corner” is. Getting them wrong cost 50× in
accuracy during development, and none of it is visible on inspection: the mask still
looks like a mask. The diagnostic, if you ever chase this: *if the error grows with the
mark’s rotation angle following `R(d) − d`, the residual `d` is a convention offset, not
noise.*

## How well it works

Validated three ways, because no single way is sufficient — synthetic scenes (exact
ground truth by construction), real photographs (round-trip through an independent
decoder), and DIBCO (hand-labelled per-pixel ink truth).

|                              | detection                           | round-trip geometry   | round-trip when *measurable*   |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------------------|
| **QR** (189 real photos)     | 80%                                 | 77%                   | **96%**                        |
| **Barcode** (56 real photos) | 95%                                 | 48%                   | **89%**                        |
| **Text** (86 real words)     | — (no locator; you supply the quad) | —                     | see below                      |

The conditional matters: **when inkmap judges an image measurable, an independent decoder
confirms the geometry 96% of the time.** Failures concentrate where the library already
says not to trust it.

On **real ink with hand-labelled ground truth** (DIBCO), eroding a *perfect* mask by one
pixel shifts the measured foreground mean by **17% of the foreground/background
contrast** — so the contamination argument is not an artefact of synthetic data.

**Text is the honest weak spot.** Placement works (IoU 0.76 with an image-derived shape)
but a glyph model with the wrong font does not (IoU 0.17). Measured directly: with the
correct font IoU is 0.997–1.000; with a wrong one, 0.46–0.80. For text, pass the actual
font or take the shape from the image.

📄 **[Methods and results]()** ([PDF]())
— the full write-up: approach, algorithms, every number, the datasets, the limits, and a
barcode defect the evaluation caught and forced a fix for (round-trip 5% → 48%).

## Large photographs: locate coarse, refine fine

Locating is a large share of the cost on big frames and scales with pixel count, so `find_all(photo, locate_scale=0.5)` (or `locate(bgr, gray, scale=0.5)`) runs the detectors on an `INTER_AREA`-downscaled copy and maps the placements back to full resolution; refinement then pins them to sub-pixel accuracy as usual, so coverage maps match the full-resolution ones. On a 4000 x 3000 photograph of a page with 8 QR codes, locating took 1,129 ms at full resolution, 288 ms at 0.5 and 152 ms at 0.35, with all 8 codes found and decoded (on a slower 2-core server, a synthetic page of the same size: 11.6 s, 2.5 s and 1.1 s).

Use it when your codes are large in the frame: a code’s modules should still span about 4 px after downscaling (`config.MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE`), i.e. 8 px at full resolution for 0.5 and about 11.5 px for 0.35. Below that the module count and pattern read off the small frame go wrong even though the code still decodes (at 2 px a 25 x 25 QR reads as 21 x 21), and refinement cannot repair a wrong model. So, with `full_res_retry=True` (the default), any coarse placement under that floor, or found but not decoded, is re-located on a full-resolution crop around it (`metadata["locate_retry"]` says why). The crops are small, but if every code needs one the speedup is gone, so pick the scale from your smallest code. With `full_res_retry=False`, placements under the floor are kept and marked `metadata["locate_undersampled"] = True`; do not trust their model. Custom locators run on the downscaled frame and must return coordinates in the frame they are given. A code the coarse pass misses entirely is not recovered, so lower the downscaling instead. The default, `None`, locates at full resolution exactly as before.

## Registration marks

Printed targets often carry plain marks with no code to decode: a solid square, or nested-square bullseyes at the corners of a sheet, as on OMR forms. `find_square_marks` finds them and returns each one’s projective centre to a small fraction of a pixel, which is what pose estimation needs:

```python
from inkmap.locate import BULLSEYE_RINGS, find_square_marks

marks = find_square_marks(gray)                 # largest first
for m in marks:
    m.centre, m.sigma_px                        # sub-pixel centre, its typical error
    m.corners                                   # (4, 2), clockwise from the top-left
    m.rings                                     # () for a solid square
bullseyes = [m for m in marks if m.ring_error(BULLSEYE_RINGS) < 0.06]
```

Nested marks are told apart by their ring ratios (bullseye 0.64/0.32, QR finder 5/7 and 3/7), which perspective barely changes. Anything square is a candidate (a QR symbol’s data modules too), so which mark is which on your layout stays with you; marks over 10% of the frame need `max_side_share=`. On synthetic sheets at up to 15% corner perspective and blur ≤ 2 px, the worst centre error is 0.13 px ([validation]()).

## Extending it

```python
inkmap.LOCATORS["mine"] = my_locator          # (bgr, gray) -> list[Placement]
inkmap.find(photo, locators=["mine", "qr_zxing"])
```

Tunable defaults live in `inkmap.config` — supersampling, ECC parameters, erosion
margin, saturation levels — as documented constants rather than inline magic numbers.

## Skills for AI agents

If you drive inkmap from an agent, the shipped skill
[`inkmap-usage`]() is the short version of
everything that is easy to get wrong: choosing a model, the corner-order trap, which of
the three 0–1 channels to use for what, and gating on measurability. Install it with
[`skill`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/skill), or just read it.

## Test data

384 real photographs of marks in the wild — 189 QR, 56 barcodes, 139 printed text —
(CC0 / public domain / CC BY / CC BY-SA), fetched on demand and cached:

```python
from inkmap import corpus

corpus.kinds()                        # {'qr': 189, 'barcode': 56, 'text': 139}
paths = corpus.fetch(kind="barcode")
print(corpus.attribution_text())      # attribution is required for CC BY / CC BY-SA
```

Synthetic scenes with **exact** ground-truth coverage — the only way to validate a 0–1
output, since no photograph comes with per-pixel truth:

```python
from inkmap import synth

scene = synth.render(my_model, perspective=0.05, blur=1.2, glare=0.3, jpeg_quality=80)
scene.image      # the degraded photograph
scene.coverage   # exact ground truth, by construction
```

## Looking at results

Coverage maps look plausible when subtly wrong, so check them:

```python
from inkmap import viz
import cv2

# original | overlay | coverage | weight
cv2.imwrite("check.png", viz.panel(photo, ink))
cv2.imwrite("grid.png", viz.overlay(photo, ink, draw_grid=True))
```

## Install notes

Hard dependencies are `numpy`, `opencv-python-headless` and `zxing-cpp` — all
permissively licensed (BSD / Apache-2.0), all pure wheels, no system libraries.

If you already have `opencv-python` or `opencv-contrib-python`, install with
`--no-deps` and keep yours: all four `opencv-*` distributions provide the same `cv2`
and conflict when more than one is installed.

`segno` is needed only to build a QR for an arbitrary payload (`inkmap[synth]`);
Pillow only for `GlyphModel` (`inkmap[text]`).

Deliberately **not** used: `qrdet` / `qreader`, which are MIT on the tin but depend on
`ultralytics`, which is AGPL-3.0.

# _autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md

# inkmap.config

Tunable defaults, in one place.

Every number the algorithms depend on lives here rather than inline, so behaviour can
be adjusted without editing logic and the meaning of each constant is documented
exactly once. Functions take these as keyword-only defaults; nothing reads the module
at call time, so overriding one is a call-site concern, not global mutable state.

### Module Attributes

| [`SUPERSAMPLES`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.SUPERSAMPLES)                  | Sub-samples per pixel per axis when computing area coverage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ECC_TEMPLATE_BLUR_FRAC`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.ECC_TEMPLATE_BLUR_FRAC)        | Gaussian smoothing of the ECC template, as a fraction of one model unit's rendered size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`ECC_MIN_CORRELATION`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.ECC_MIN_CORRELATION)           | Minimum ECC correlation for a refinement to be accepted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`ECC_MIN_SCALE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.ECC_MIN_SCALE)                 | The template is rendered at the observed pixels-per-unit, clamped here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`TEMPLATE_MARGIN_UNITS`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.TEMPLATE_MARGIN_UNITS)         | Clear margin rendered around the ECC template, in model units.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`MARGIN_UNITS`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARGIN_UNITS)                  | Default clear margin around a mark, in model units, labelled Region.MARGIN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`PURE_COVERAGE_TOL`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.PURE_COVERAGE_TOL)             | Coverage within this of 1.0 (or 0.0) counts as pure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`EDGE_MARGIN_SIGMAS`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.EDGE_MARGIN_SIGMAS)            | Default erosion of the pure-foreground mask, in multiples of the estimated blur sigma.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`DEFAULT_BLUR_SIGMA`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.DEFAULT_BLUR_SIGMA)            | Fallback blur sigma (px) when it cannot be estimated from the image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`MIN_SCALE_OVER_SIGMA`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MIN_SCALE_OVER_SIGMA)          | Below this ratio of pixels-per-unit to blur sigma, no erosion can recover an uncontaminated measurement -- the blur is wide relative to a unit and every pixel is mixed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`SATURATION_LEVEL`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.SATURATION_LEVEL)              | Pixels at or above this 8-bit level are treated as clipped and excluded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`BLACK_CLIP_LEVEL`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.BLACK_CLIP_LEVEL)              | Pixels at or below this level are treated as crushed black and excluded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`DEFAULT_LOCATORS`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.DEFAULT_LOCATORS)              | Locator strategies tried by default, in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`LOCATE_RETRY_PADDING`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.LOCATE_RETRY_PADDING)          | a coarse placement that was not decoded, or is under `MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE`, is retried on a full-resolution crop around it, padded on each side by this fraction of the placement's larger bounding-box side.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE) | below this many image pixels per model feature (a QR module, a barcode's narrowest bar) *in the downscaled frame*, the model a locator reads off that frame is unreliable even when the code decodes -- with modules at 2 px a 25 x 25 QR is read as 21 x 21, at 2.5-3.5 px tens of its 625 modules flip, and only from 4 px are they all right (synthetic pages, `locate(scale=0.5)`). |
| [`MARK_DARK_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_DARK_SHARE)               | A pixel is foreground when it is darker than this share of the local mean brightness.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`MARK_MIN_CONTRAST`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_CONTRAST)             | ...and darker than the local mean by at least this many grey levels (of 255).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`MARK_LOCAL_WINDOW_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_LOCAL_WINDOW_SHARE)       | wider than any mark, so a mark's own ink does not raise the threshold inside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`MARK_BORDER_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_BORDER_PX)                | A contour within this many pixels of the frame's edge is cut by it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`MARK_POLY_EPSILON_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_POLY_EPSILON_SHARE)       | A contour is a quadrilateral when a polygon within this share of its perimeter fits it with four vertices (`cv2.approxPolyDP`'s epsilon).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`MARK_MAX_SIDE_RATIO`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_SIDE_RATIO)           | A quadrilateral whose opposite sides differ by more than this factor is not a square seen at any plausible incidence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`MARK_MIN_HOLE_AREA_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_HOLE_AREA_SHARE)      | the square is solid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`MARK_CORNER_TRIM_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_CORNER_TRIM_SHARE)        | Contour points within this share of a side's length from either corner are left out of that side's line fit: the corner is where binarisation rounds the outline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`MARK_EDGE_PROFILE_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_PROFILE_PX)          | Each side's line is refined against the grey image along profiles this many pixels either side of it (and no more than MARK_EDGE_PROFILE_SHARE of the side's length), long enough to bracket a blurred edge, short enough not to reach a ring's next edge.                                                                                                                              |
| [`MARK_EDGE_STEP_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_STEP_PX)             | Spacing of the samples along each edge profile, in pixels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| [`MARK_EDGE_ITERATIONS`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_ITERATIONS)          | Refinement passes per side.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`MARK_EDGE_OUTLIER_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_OUTLIER_PX)          | A refined edge crossing further than this from the fitted line (or three times the line's scatter, if larger) is an outlier -- a glare bite, a speck -- and is refitted without.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`MARK_MAX_SIDE_SCATTER_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_SIDE_SCATTER_PX)      | A quadrilateral whose refined sides scatter about their lines by more than this (rms, in pixels), or this share of its side if larger, is not a square: a disc's outline also fits four lines, but its scatter grows with its size (0.35 px for a 10 px radius, 1 px for 20 px), where a square's stays at the noise floor.                                                             |
| [`MARK_MIN_QUAD_SIDE_PX`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_QUAD_SIDE_PX)         | The smallest square considered at all, in pixels on a side.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`MARK_WINDOW_OVER_MAX_SIDE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_WINDOW_OVER_MAX_SIDE)     | The local-mean window is kept at least this many times the largest mark looked for (`max_side_share`): a mark wider than the window raises its own threshold and is hollowed by its own ink.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`MARK_NESTED_HOLE_AREA_RATIO`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_NESTED_HOLE_AREA_RATIO)   | A square in a hole less than this many times its own area is the inner square of a nested mark (a bullseye's hole is 4x its inner square, a QR finder's 2.8x), not a mark of its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`MARK_MAX_ASPECT`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_ASPECT)               | A quadrilateral whose mean opposite-side lengths differ by more than this factor is a rectangle, not a square: 1.6 is a square seen at about 51 degrees of incidence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`MARK_CLIP_GUARD_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_CLIP_GUARD_SHARE)         | A solid square whose neighbourhood out to this many sides runs off the frame, and holds more than MARK_CLIP_GUARD_INK_SHARE foreground, may be the inner square of a nested mark the frame cuts, and is dropped.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`MARK_RING_SPREAD_SHARE`](_autosummary/inkmap.config.html.md#inkmap.config.MARK_RING_SPREAD_SHARE)        | `sigma_px` calibration, fitted on synthetic sheets (rotations, perspective up to 0.15, blur 0.7-1.5 px, noise 1-4) so that the median centre error is about sigma for both kinds of mark.                                                                                                                                                                                               |

### inkmap.config.BLACK_CLIP_LEVEL *= 2*

Pixels at or below this level are treated as crushed black and excluded.

### inkmap.config.DEFAULT_BLUR_SIGMA *= 1.0*

Fallback blur sigma (px) when it cannot be estimated from the image.

### inkmap.config.DEFAULT_LOCATORS *= ('qr_zxing', 'qr_aruco', 'qr_opencv', 'barcode_zxing')*

Locator strategies tried by default, in order. Measured on 189 real photographs of
QR codes: zxing 74%, aruco 68%, opencv 43%, union 80% – the cascade is worth ~37
points of recall over OpenCV alone.

### inkmap.config.ECC_MIN_CORRELATION *= 0.5*

Minimum ECC correlation for a refinement to be accepted. Below this the refined
transform is discarded and the locator’s own corners kept.

### inkmap.config.ECC_MIN_SCALE *= 2*

The template is rendered at the observed pixels-per-unit, clamped here. Matching the
observed scale matters: rendering far below it aliases the comparison and the
refinement gets *worse* than the unrefined corners.

### inkmap.config.ECC_TEMPLATE_BLUR_FRAC *= 0.25*

Gaussian smoothing of the ECC template, as a fraction of one model unit’s rendered
size. Photographed edges are soft; a perfectly sharp template correlates poorly.

### inkmap.config.EDGE_MARGIN_SIGMAS *= 2.0*

Default erosion of the pure-foreground mask, in multiples of the estimated blur
sigma. The point spread function spreads signal across boundaries, so geometric
purity is necessary but not sufficient. ~2 sigma holds bias below 0.5%, ~3 below 0.1%.

### inkmap.config.LOCATE_RETRY_PADDING *= 0.5*

a coarse placement that was
not decoded, or is under `MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE`, is retried on a full-resolution crop around it, padded on each
side by this fraction of the placement’s larger bounding-box side. 0.5 comfortably
holds a QR quiet zone (4 modules of a symbol at least 21 wide) plus the coarse
pass’s position error, while keeping the crop a small fraction of the frame.

* **Type:**
  Coarse-to-fine locating (`locate(..., scale=s)`)

### inkmap.config.MARGIN_UNITS *= 4.0*

Default clear margin around a mark, in model units, labelled Region.MARGIN.
4 matches the QR quiet zone required by ISO/IEC 18004.

### inkmap.config.MARK_BORDER_PX *= 2*

A contour within this many pixels of the frame’s edge is cut by it. Its shape is not
the mark’s, and a clipped mark’s centre is wrong by a share of its side, so it is
dropped rather than measured.

### inkmap.config.MARK_CLIP_GUARD_SHARE *= 1.2*

A solid square whose neighbourhood out to this many sides runs off the frame, and
holds more than MARK_CLIP_GUARD_INK_SHARE foreground, may be the inner square of a
nested mark the frame cuts, and is dropped. A bullseye’s outer edge is 1.06 inner
sides out from its inner square, a QR finder’s 0.67.

### inkmap.config.MARK_CORNER_TRIM_SHARE *= 0.15*

Contour points within this share of a side’s length from either corner are left out
of that side’s line fit: the corner is where binarisation rounds the outline.

### inkmap.config.MARK_DARK_SHARE *= 0.72*

A pixel is foreground when it is darker than this share of the local mean
brightness. Relative rather than absolute, so that an unevenly lit sheet (3.5:1 from
one side to the other) and a dim frame are binarised alike.

### inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_ITERATIONS *= 2*

Refinement passes per side. The first takes the line from the contour’s quantised
position to the edge; the second re-centres the profiles on it.

### inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_OUTLIER_PX *= 0.75*

A refined edge crossing further than this from the fitted line (or three times the
line’s scatter, if larger) is an outlier – a glare bite, a speck – and is refitted
without.

### inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_PROFILE_PX *= 2.5*

Each side’s line is refined against the grey image along profiles this many pixels
either side of it (and no more than MARK_EDGE_PROFILE_SHARE of the side’s length),
long enough to bracket a blurred edge, short enough not to reach a ring’s next edge.

### inkmap.config.MARK_EDGE_STEP_PX *= 0.25*

Spacing of the samples along each edge profile, in pixels.

### inkmap.config.MARK_LOCAL_WINDOW_SHARE *= 0.12*

wider
than any mark, so a mark’s own ink does not raise the threshold inside it.

* **Type:**
  The local mean is taken over a window this share of the frame’s shorter side

### inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_ASPECT *= 1.6*

A quadrilateral whose mean opposite-side lengths differ by more than this factor is
a rectangle, not a square: 1.6 is a square seen at about 51 degrees of incidence.

### inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_SIDE_RATIO *= 2.5*

A quadrilateral whose opposite sides differ by more than this factor is not a square
seen at any plausible incidence.

### inkmap.config.MARK_MAX_SIDE_SCATTER_PX *= 0.25*

A quadrilateral whose refined sides scatter about their lines by more than this
(rms, in pixels), or this share of its side if larger, is not a square: a disc’s
outline also fits four lines, but its scatter grows with its size (0.35 px for a
10 px radius, 1 px for 20 px), where a square’s stays at the noise floor. A disc
under ~10 px radius cannot be told from a square this way.

### inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_CONTRAST *= 6.0*

…and darker than the local mean by at least this many grey levels (of 255).
Without a floor, sensor noise on a near-black table is “darker than 72% of the local
mean” everywhere, and the contour search drowns in blobs.

### inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_HOLE_AREA_SHARE *= 0.02*

the square is solid.

* **Type:**
  A hole smaller than this share of its square’s area is noise

### inkmap.config.MARK_MIN_QUAD_SIDE_PX *= 5.0*

The smallest square considered at all, in pixels on a side. Lower than any mark’s
own `min_side_px`, because a nested mark’s inner square is a third of its side and
must be found for the mark to be.

### inkmap.config.MARK_NESTED_HOLE_AREA_RATIO *= 9.0*

A square in a hole less than this many times its own area is the inner square of a
nested mark (a bullseye’s hole is 4x its inner square, a QR finder’s 2.8x), not a
mark of its own. A sheet’s outline or a form’s box holds its marks in a far larger
hole.

### inkmap.config.MARK_POLY_EPSILON_SHARE *= 0.04*

A contour is a quadrilateral when a polygon within this share of its perimeter fits
it with four vertices (`cv2.approxPolyDP`’s epsilon).

### inkmap.config.MARK_RING_SPREAD_SHARE *= 0.5*

`sigma_px` calibration, fitted on synthetic sheets (rotations, perspective up to
0.15, blur 0.7-1.5 px, noise 1-4) so that the median centre error is about sigma for
both kinds of mark. A nested mark’s term is this share of the rms distance of its
squares’ centres from their mean; a solid mark, with nothing to disagree with, gets
this floor (its side-fit scatter alone understated its error ~4x).

### inkmap.config.MARK_WINDOW_OVER_MAX_SIDE *= 1.2*

The local-mean window is kept at least this many times the largest mark looked for
(`max_side_share`): a mark wider than the window raises its own threshold and is
hollowed by its own ink.

### inkmap.config.MIN_COARSE_PIXELS_PER_FEATURE *= 4.0*

below this many image pixels per model feature (a QR
module, a barcode’s narrowest bar) *in the downscaled frame*, the model a locator
reads off that frame is unreliable even when the code decodes – with modules at
2 px a 25 x 25 QR is read as 21 x 21, at 2.5-3.5 px tens of its 625 modules flip,
and only from 4 px are they all right (synthetic pages, `locate(scale=0.5)`).
Such placements are re-located on a full-resolution crop. See `locate`.

* **Type:**
  Coarse-to-fine locating

### inkmap.config.MIN_SCALE_OVER_SIGMA *= 6.0*

Below this ratio of pixels-per-unit to blur sigma, no erosion can recover an
uncontaminated measurement – the blur is wide relative to a unit and every pixel is
mixed. Results are flagged rather than silently returned. See docs/validation.md.

### inkmap.config.PURE_COVERAGE_TOL *= 0.001*

Coverage within this of 1.0 (or 0.0) counts as pure. Not exactly 1.0, to tolerate
float rounding in the raster.

### inkmap.config.SATURATION_LEVEL *= 250*

Pixels at or above this 8-bit level are treated as clipped and excluded.

### inkmap.config.SUPERSAMPLES *= 8*

Sub-samples per pixel per axis when computing area coverage. A pixel’s coverage is
quantised to 1/SUPERSAMPLES\*\*2, so 4 -> 17 levels, 8 -> 65. Below 4 the quantisation
itself becomes a bias source.

### inkmap.config.TEMPLATE_MARGIN_UNITS *= 2.0*

Clear margin rendered around the ECC template, in model units. Without it the blur
kernel reflects interior content across the border and biases alignment ~0.45 px.


# _autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md

# inkmap.corpus

The real-photograph test corpus: 384 photographed marks in the wild, from Wikimedia Commons.

189 QR codes, 56 linear barcodes and 139 images of printed text – signs, posters,
packaging, business cards, stickers, billboards, menus, tickets, screens, inscriptions.

Synthetic scenes ([`inkmap.synth`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#module-inkmap.synth)) are the only way to validate a *coverage* value,
because no photograph comes with per-pixel ink ground truth. But synthetic scenes cannot
tell you whether detection survives a mark printed on a curved bottle under a sodium
lamp. The two test sets answer different questions and you need both.

Only the manifest ships with the package – titles, URLs, licences and attribution,
about 200 KB. The images are fetched on demand and cached, because a few hundred MB of
photographs has no business inside a wheel, and because redistributing them would mean
carrying every attribution requirement into this repository.

Every image is CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA. Attribution is in the manifest and
[`attribution_text()`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.attribution_text) will render it – if you publish results using these images,
use it.

> from inkmap import corpus

> corpus.kinds()                          # {‘qr’: 189, ‘barcode’: 56, ‘text’: 139}
> paths = corpus.fetch(kind=”barcode”)    # download + cache, returns local paths
> for path, meta in corpus.items(kind=”qr”):

> > …

### Module Attributes

| [`MANIFEST`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.MANIFEST)   | kind (qr/barcode/text), file, title, url, source, license, artist.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`kinds`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.kinds)()                                        | How many records of each mark kind the manifest holds.                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cache_dir`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.cache_dir)()                                    | Where fetched images live.                                                     |
| [`fetch`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.fetch)(\*[, kind, limit, dest, pace, attempts]) | Download the corpus (skipping anything already cached) and return local paths. |
| [`items`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.items)(\*[, kind, dest])                        | Yield `(path, record)` for every cached corpus image, optionally by kind.      |
| [`attribution_text`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#inkmap.corpus.attribution_text)([records])                    | Render the attribution block required by the CC BY / CC BY-SA images.          |

### inkmap.corpus.cache_dir()

Where fetched images live.

Honours `INKMAP_CORPUS_DIR`, else the XDG cache location. Test data is neither code
nor user configuration, so it does not belong beside the package: a wheel install
would make the package directory read-only, and a reinstall would silently discard
a 120 MB download.

### inkmap.corpus.fetch(, kind=None, limit=None, dest=None, pace=1.1, attempts=5)

Download the corpus (skipping anything already cached) and return local paths.

Commons rate-limits hard and answers with HTTP 429 rather than queueing, so
requests are paced and retried with exponential backoff. A full cold fetch takes
several minutes; it is incremental, so interrupting and re-running is safe.
