# _autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md

# inkmap.photometry

Turning masks into measurements that are actually valid.

Everything here exists because a per-pixel mask is necessary but nowhere near
sufficient for measuring anything *about* the mark – its reflectance, its density, its
colour, how much of it actually printed. The failure modes are silent: they do not
raise, they return a plausible number wrong by tens of percent.

Measured on synthetic scenes with exact ground truth (see `docs/validation.md`), the
bias in recovering a foreground-only signal at 6 px per model unit:

| pixel selection   | blur=0   | sigma=1 px   | sigma=2 px   | sigma=3 px   |
|-------------------|----------|--------------|--------------|--------------|
| coverage > 0.5    | -3.3%    | -12.2%       | -23.3%       | -32.4%       |
| coverage == 1.0   | -0.0%    | -8.0%        | -19.9%       | -30.1%       |
| weight (2 sigma)  | +0.0%    | -0.2%        | -0.6%        | -1.5%        |

Two lessons. Geometric purity is necessary but *not* sufficient – a pixel entirely
under foreground still reads 30% low, because the point spread function drags
background signal into it, and that contamination has a different footprint from
partial area coverage. Only spatial erosion removes it, which is what the weight
channel is.

And erosion stops working once the blur is wide relative to a model unit: there are no
uncontaminated pixels left. That is the classic partial-volume result, and it is why
[`measurability()`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.measurability) exists – better to say the measurement is not possible than to
return a confidently wrong number.

### Functions

| [`srgb_to_linear`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.srgb_to_linear)(image)                              | Undo the sRGB transfer function, returning float in `[0, 1]`.                  |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`measurement_mask`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.measurement_mask)(ink_map, \*[, kind, purity, ...]) | Pixels safe to measure: geometrically pure, then eroded clear of edges.        |
| [`measurement_margin`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.measurement_margin)(blur_sigma, \*[, sigmas])       | Erosion radius in pixels for a given blur sigma.                               |
| [`measurability`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.measurability)(ink_map, \*[, min_pixels])           | Judge whether a foreground/background measurement can be trusted here.         |
| [`measure`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.measure)(image, ink_map, \*[, linearize, ...])      | Aggregate `image` over the safe foreground and background pixels of `ink_map`. |
| [`illumination_field`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.illumination_field)(image, ink_map, \*[, degree])   | Fit a smooth illumination field across the mark from its background pixels.    |

### Classes

| [`Measurability`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.Measurability)(ok, pixels_per_feature, ...[, ...])   | Whether a trustworthy measurement is possible on this image at all.           |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Measurement`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.Measurement)(foreground_mean, foreground_std, ...)   | Aggregated signal over foreground and background, with its validity attached. |

### *class* inkmap.photometry.Measurability(ok, pixels_per_feature, blur_sigma, resolution_ratio, n_foreground_pixels, n_background_pixels, reasons=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Whether a trustworthy measurement is possible on this image at all.

#### resolution_ratio *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

`pixels_per_feature / blur_sigma`. Below ~6 the blur is wide relative to the
mark’s smallest feature and no erosion leaves uncontaminated pixels.

### *class* inkmap.photometry.Measurement(foreground_mean, foreground_std, foreground_median, background_mean, background_std, background_median, n_foreground, n_background, measurability=None, metadata=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Aggregated signal over foreground and background, with its validity attached.

`measurability` is carried along deliberately: a caller that ignores it has to do
so explicitly.

#### *property* contrast *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Foreground minus background.

#### *property* ratio *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Foreground over background; `nan` when the background reads zero.

#### *property* snr *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Contrast over the pooled standard deviation.

### inkmap.photometry.illumination_field(image, ink_map, , degree=1)

Fit a smooth illumination field across the mark from its background pixels.

The background within the mark samples the illumination across the whole mark, so
the scene calibrates itself – no flat-field frame required. A first-order (planar)
fit handles the usual oblique-lighting gradient; degree 2 handles vignetting
curvature at the cost of being able to absorb real signal.

Returns a field normalised to mean 1.0 over the mark; divide by it to flatten.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.photometry.measurability(ink_map, , min_pixels=50)

Judge whether a foreground/background measurement can be trusted here.

Returning a number quietly biased by 30% is worse than refusing, so this is checked
up front and attached to every [`Measurement`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.Measurement).

* **Return type:**
  [`Measurability`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.Measurability)

### inkmap.photometry.measure(image, ink_map, , linearize=True, flatten=False, margin=None, robust=True)

Aggregate `image` over the safe foreground and background pixels of `ink_map`.

`image` need not be the one the mark was located in: any frame registered to it
works, which is the usual way to measure a different exposure, channel or modality
using geometry established once on the sharpest frame.

`linearize` undoes sRGB encoding first – leave it on for anything from a normal
camera pipeline, off for already-linear data. `flatten` divides out a fitted
illumination field. `robust` reports medians alongside means; on real photographs
they diverge exactly where something is wrong, which makes the pair a free
diagnostic.

* **Return type:**
  [`Measurement`](_autosummary/inkmap.photometry.html.md#inkmap.photometry.Measurement)

### inkmap.photometry.measurement_margin(blur_sigma, , sigmas=2.0)

Erosion radius in pixels for a given blur sigma. At least 1 px.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### inkmap.photometry.measurement_mask(ink_map, , kind='foreground', purity=0.999, margin=None)

Pixels safe to measure: geometrically pure, then eroded clear of edges.

`kind` selects `"foreground"` or `"background"`. `purity` is the coverage
threshold for “pure”; the default demands essentially total coverage, which is the
point – a partially covered pixel biases the mean toward the other class.

This is the mask to use for a measurement. `InkMap.foreground_mask()` is for
display and for anything that only needs a label.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.photometry.srgb_to_linear(image)

Undo the sRGB transfer function, returning float in `[0, 1]`.

Averaging pixel values without this is a real error, not a nicety: sRGB values are
perceptually encoded, so the mean of encoded values is not the encoded mean
intensity. Any difference between two exposures compounds it. Apply before any
arithmetic that claims to be about light.

The piecewise IEC 61966-2-1 curve, not the 2.2 power approximation.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md

# inkmap.synth

Synthetic scenes with exact ground truth.

Real photographs cannot validate a coverage map. Nobody can hand-label what fraction of
a pixel is foreground, and no public dataset carries per-pixel coverage ground truth for
printed marks – the document-binarisation benchmarks (DIBCO) are binary. So the only
way to measure whether a 0..1 output is *right* is to render scenes whose true coverage
is known analytically.

The trick that makes it exact: render the image *from* the coverage map. Supersample the
model through a known transform to get true coverage, then form the clean image as
`255 * (1 - coverage)`. Ground truth and stimulus are the same object by construction,
and any degradation applied afterwards (blur, noise, gradient, glare, JPEG) leaves the
ground truth correct.

Works for any model, so a text or logo pipeline is validated the same way as a QR one.
Real photographs remain essential for *detection* rate – see [`inkmap.corpus`](_autosummary/inkmap.corpus.html.md#module-inkmap.corpus).

### Functions

| [`render`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.render)([model, size, pixels_per_unit, ...])      | Render one synthetic photograph of `model` with exact ground-truth coverage.                                           |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`qr_model`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.qr_model)([payload, error])                       | A QR [`MatrixModel`](_autosummary/inkmap.models.html.md#inkmap.models.MatrixModel), from `payload` via segno. |
| [`default_matrix`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.default_matrix)()                                 | The shipped QR module matrix (a real version-3 symbol), True = dark module.                                            |
| [`degrade`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.degrade)(image, \*[, blur, noise, gradient, ...]) | Apply a capture-order degradation chain to a float image, returning uint8.                                             |
| [`nested_square`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.nested_square)(side[, rings])                     | A square mark as a `(side, side)` cell grid: foreground, then alternating rings.                                       |
| [`mark_sheet`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.mark_sheet)()                                     | A card of square registration marks, and where each one's centre truly is.                                             |

### Classes

| [`Scene`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.Scene)(image, coverage, transform, model[, ...])   | A synthetic image together with the truth used to make it.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* inkmap.synth.Scene(image, coverage, transform, model, params=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A synthetic image together with the truth used to make it.

#### coverage *: ndarray*

(H, W) float32 exact foreground area coverage.

#### image *: ndarray*

(H, W) uint8 grayscale.

#### transform *: ndarray*

(3, 3) true model -> image mapping.

### inkmap.synth.default_matrix()

The shipped QR module matrix (a real version-3 symbol), True = dark module.

Shipped so that [`render()`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.render) – and therefore the test suite and every example –
works on a bare `pip install inkmap`, with no optional dependency.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.synth.degrade(image, , blur=0.0, noise=0.0, gradient=0.0, glare=0.0, jpeg_quality=None, rng=None)

Apply a capture-order degradation chain to a float image, returning uint8.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.synth.mark_sheet()

A card of square registration marks, and where each one’s centre truly is.

Three bullseyes and a solid square at the corners, as on an OMR form, and two QR
finder patterns inside: 700 x 500 cells, marks 50 cells (42 for a finder). Render it
with [`render()`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.render) at about 1.2 pixels per cell for ~60 px marks. Returns
`(model, truth)`, `truth` being `(centre_uv, rings)` per mark in model units,
so `cv2.perspectiveTransform` through a scene’s transform gives the true image
centres.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`MatrixModel`](_autosummary/inkmap.models.grid.html.md#inkmap.models.grid.MatrixModel), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)]]]

### inkmap.synth.nested_square(side, rings=())

A square mark as a `(side, side)` cell grid: foreground, then alternating rings.

`rings` are the sides of the nested squares as fractions of `side`, outermost
first, alternating background and foreground. Each must leave an equal whole number
of cells on both sides, or the mark would be off-centre – that is an error.

```pycon
>>> nested_square(7, (5 / 7, 3 / 7)).astype(int)[3]
array([1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1])
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.synth.qr_model(payload=None, , error='m')

A QR [`MatrixModel`](_autosummary/inkmap.models.html.md#inkmap.models.MatrixModel), from `payload` via segno.

With no payload, uses the shipped matrix and needs no dependency. Uses
`segno.make_qr` rather than `segno.make`: the latter may return a Micro QR for
short payloads, a different symbology with different module counts.

* **Return type:**
  [`MatrixModel`](_autosummary/inkmap.models.grid.html.md#inkmap.models.grid.MatrixModel)

### inkmap.synth.render(model=None, , size=800, pixels_per_unit=10.0, perspective=0.0, rotation=0.0, blur=0.0, noise=0.0, gradient=0.0, glare=0.0, jpeg_quality=None, samples=8, rng=None)

Render one synthetic photograph of `model` with exact ground-truth coverage.

Degradations are applied in capture order – geometry, then optics (blur, glare),
then illumination, then sensor noise, then compression – because any other order
models a camera that does not exist. `perspective` jitters the four corners by
that fraction of the mark’s span; `rotation` is in degrees; `gradient` is the
fractional illumination falloff across the frame.

* **Return type:**
  [`Scene`](_autosummary/inkmap.synth.html.md#inkmap.synth.Scene)


# _autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md

# inkmap.types

The data types the whole package speaks in.

Naming here is deliberate, because the obvious names are traps:

* The two classes inside a mark’s footprint are `FOREGROUND` and `BACKGROUND`,
  **not** dark and light. Dark/light describe *appearance*, and appearance inverts:
  white-on-black print, reflectance-reversed symbols (explicitly permitted by ISO/IEC
  18004 for QR), and any inverted imaging modality all swap which class is dark. A
  `dark_mask` would then silently mean foreground in one image and background in the
  next. [`Polarity`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Polarity) carries that mapping explicitly instead.
* `BACKGROUND` is scoped to *within the mark’s footprint*. The clear margin around
  the mark is `MARGIN` and everything else is `OUTSIDE`, so the ambiguity that
  makes a bare “background” dangerous – substrate inside the mark, or everything that
  is not the mark? – cannot arise.
* The continuous value is `coverage`, after ISO 12647-2:2013 3.1 *area coverage*,
  “ratio of the area covered with ink to the entire area” – the only term in any
  standard whose definition is literally the quantity computed here.

See `docs/terminology.md` for the full cross-field mapping.

### Classes

| [`InkMap`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.InkMap)(coverage, region, placement[, ...])        | Per-pixel foreground coverage for one placement, plus the geometry it came from.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Placement`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Placement)(model, transform, quad[, locator, ...]) | A located instance of a model: which shape, and where it sits in the image.        |
| [`Polarity`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Polarity)(\*values)                                | Which apparent-brightness state the foreground corresponds to.                     |
| [`Region`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Region)(\*values)                                  | Four-way pixel classification.                                                     |

### *class* inkmap.types.InkMap(coverage, region, placement, polarity=Polarity.FOREGROUND_IS_DARK, weight=None, blur_sigma=None, metadata=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Per-pixel foreground coverage for one placement, plus the geometry it came from.

`coverage` is *geometric* area coverage: the fraction of each pixel’s area lying
under foreground. It is not an optical/reflectance-derived coverage (which lateral
light scattering in the substrate inflates – the Murray-Davies/Yule-Nielsen
effect), and it is not a probability. See `confidence()` for that.

#### background_mask(, threshold=0.5)

Bare-substrate pixels within the mark’s footprint (not the margin).

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

#### blur_sigma *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

Estimated image blur (px). `nan` means estimation failed – typically because
the modelled shape and the photograph do not correspond.

#### coverage *: ndarray*

(H, W) float32 in [0, 1]. Zero outside the mark.

#### foreground_mask(, threshold=0.5)

Boolean foreground mask by thresholding coverage. Fine for display and
labelling; for anything photometric use [`inkmap.measurement_mask()`](_autosummary/inkmap.html.md#inkmap.measurement_mask)
instead, which accounts for blur.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

#### inside_mask(, margin=False)

Every pixel within the mark’s footprint. With `margin=True`, include the
clear surround as well.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

#### margin_mask()

The clear surround – an alternative reference region.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

#### region *: ndarray*

(H, W) uint8 of [`Region`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Region) values.

#### weight *: ndarray | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

(H, W) float32 in [0, 1] – the blur-aware measurement weight, and the **only**
channel that should gate a physical measurement. Coverage is geometric and ignores
the point spread function; confidence is epistemic and says nothing about
partial-area contamination. See [`inkmap.coverage.measurement_weight()`](_autosummary/inkmap.coverage.html.md#inkmap.coverage.measurement_weight).

### *class* inkmap.types.Placement(model, transform, quad, locator='', payload=None, refined=False, score=None, metadata=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A located instance of a model: which shape, and where it sits in the image.

`transform` is the bridge the whole package is built on – a 3x3 homography from
*model space* (the model’s own units, origin at its top-left) to image pixels. The
quad is just its image under that transform, kept for convenience.

#### locator *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= ''*

Which locator strategy produced this.

#### payload *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

Decoded content, when the locator happened to decode something. Never required:
decoding is not the point, and a barely-deposited mark may locate but not decode.

#### *property* pixels_per_feature *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Image pixels across the model’s smallest feature.

**This** is the resolution figure that governs whether a trustworthy
measurement is possible – not [`pixels_per_unit`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Placement.pixels_per_unit). A model unit is not a
feature: a QR module is both, but a glyph rendered onto a 512-cell raster has
strokes tens of cells wide, so pixels-per-unit there would understate the real
resolution by that factor and declare every image unmeasurable.

#### *property* pixels_per_unit *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Image pixels per model unit.

For a QR symbol a “unit” is one module; for a barcode, one narrow bar; for a
raster model, one raster cell. Use [`pixels_per_feature`](_autosummary/inkmap.types.html.md#inkmap.types.Placement.pixels_per_feature) to reason about
whether the image resolves the mark.

#### quad *: ndarray*

(4, 2) float32 image-space corners of the model’s extent, in the *model’s* own
order (its top-left first), not re-sorted into image order. Re-sorting by
coordinate sum/difference – a common idiom – silently mislabels corners once the
mark is rotated past 45 degrees, which rotates the model and corrupts every derived
mask while leaving it looking plausible.

#### score *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

Alignment score from refinement, if it ran. A proxy for geometric fit quality.

#### transform *: ndarray*

(3, 3) float64, model coordinates -> image pixels.

#### *property* units_per_pixel *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Model units spanned by one image pixel, averaged over the two axes.

### *class* inkmap.types.Polarity(\*values)

Bases: [`IntEnum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.IntEnum)

Which apparent-brightness state the foreground corresponds to.

Carried explicitly so that no appearance word ever has to stand in for a physical
class. Flipping this is the supported way to handle inverted print and inverted
imaging, rather than inverting masks at the call site.

#### FOREGROUND_IS_DARK *= 0*

ink absorbs, so the mark reads darker than the substrate.

* **Type:**
  The usual case

#### FOREGROUND_IS_LIGHT *= 1*

the mark reads brighter than the substrate.

* **Type:**
  Reversed

### *class* inkmap.types.Region(\*values)

Bases: [`IntEnum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.IntEnum)

Four-way pixel classification.

Not a matting *trimap*: a trimap’s third class is “unknown/undecided”, whereas
every class here is a decided statement about location.

#### BACKGROUND *= 2*

Bare substrate within the mark’s footprint.

#### FOREGROUND *= 3*

The mark itself – printed ink, toner, engraving, whatever laid it down.

#### MARGIN *= 1*

The clear surround a mark is specified to have – a QR quiet zone, a barcode
light margin, the whitespace around a glyph. Guaranteed background, contiguous, and
free of edge effects from neighbouring foreground, which often makes it a better
reference region than the background *inside* the mark.

#### OUTSIDE *= 0*

Outside the mark and its margin.


# _autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md

# inkmap.viz

Visual overlays, for checking that a result is actually right.

Coverage maps are the kind of output that looks plausible when it is subtly wrong – a
half-unit offset or a quarter-turn rotation of the model both produce a mask of the
right shape, size and density. Looking at it is the cheapest way to catch that class of
error, so this is a first-class part of the workflow rather than a nicety.

Only needs OpenCV and numpy; nothing here imports matplotlib.

### Module Attributes

| [`REGION_COLORS`](_autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md#inkmap.viz.REGION_COLORS)   | BGR colours per region.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|

### Functions

| [`overlay`](_autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md#inkmap.viz.overlay)(image, ink_map, \*[, alpha, ...])   | Blend the region map over the original image.                                |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`panel`](_autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md#inkmap.viz.panel)(image, ink_map, \*[, crop])           | Four-pane contact sheet: original | overlay | coverage | measurement weight. |
| [`colorize_coverage`](_autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md#inkmap.viz.colorize_coverage)(coverage)                 | (H, W) float coverage -> BGR heatmap.                                        |
| [`colorize_regions`](_autosummary/inkmap.viz.html.md#inkmap.viz.colorize_regions)(region)                    | (H, W) region labels -> BGR image.                                           |

### inkmap.viz.REGION_COLORS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]* *= {Region.OUTSIDE: (0, 0, 0), Region.MARGIN: (90, 90, 90), Region.BACKGROUND: (200, 140, 60), Region.FOREGROUND: (60, 90, 230)}*

BGR colours per region. Foreground warm, background cool, margin neutral.

### inkmap.viz.colorize_coverage(coverage)

(H, W) float coverage -> BGR heatmap. Partial coverage is what to look at.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.viz.colorize_regions(region)

(H, W) region labels -> BGR image.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.viz.overlay(image, ink_map, , alpha=0.45, draw_quad=True, draw_grid=False)

Blend the region map over the original image.

`draw_grid` overlays the fitted model grid, which is the fastest way to see a
mis-fitted transform: if the lines do not sit on the mark’s own boundaries, every
downstream number is wrong no matter how clean the mask looks.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### inkmap.viz.panel(image, ink_map, , crop=True)

Four-pane contact sheet: original | overlay | coverage | measurement weight.

The last two panes are the ones worth studying. Coverage should show a thin soft
fringe along every foreground boundary; weight should show that fringe eaten away,
leaving only interiors. If weight is empty, the image cannot support a measurement.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`inkmap` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `inkmap-usage`

Use when you need per-pixel foreground/background separation of a printed mark in a photograph — a QR code, barcode, printed text, logo, or any shape you can model — or when you need to MEASURE something about the mark itself (its reflectance, density, colour, how much of it actually printed) rather than decode it. Triggers on “which pixels are the ink”, “segment the QR code”, “measure the printed area”, “ink coverage”, “foreground mask for this mark”, “is this print defective”, “compare two exposures of a label”, “subpixel mask”, “measure the barcode not read it”. Covers choosing a model, the corner-order trap, which of the three 0–1 channels to use for what, and the measurability gate that stops you reporting a number biased by tens of percent.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/inkmap inkmap-usage --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`inkmap/data/skills/inkmap-usage`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/inkmap/tree/HEAD/inkmap/data/skills/inkmap-usage) (bundled with the pip package).

### `inkmap-dev-validation`

Read before changing anything in inkmap that could move a number — geometry, coverage rasterisation, refinement, blur estimation, measurement weighting, or a locator — and before regenerating docs/methods-and-results.md or docs/validation.md. Covers the three validation tiers (synthetic ground truth, real-photograph round-trip, corpus detection), how to run each, which numbers live in which document, and the half-pixel convention failures that any of these changes can silently reintroduce. Triggers on “regenerate the benchmarks”, “update the validation numbers”, “the report is stale”, “did that change accuracy”, or any edit to coverage.py / geometry.py / models/ / locate/.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/inkmap inkmap-dev-validation --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/inkmap-dev-validation`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/inkmap/tree/HEAD/skills/inkmap-dev-validation).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install inkmap`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/inkmap/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`inkmap.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/inkmap/inkmap.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/inkmap/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)


# api.html.md

# API reference

| [`inkmap`](_autosummary/inkmap.html.md#module-inkmap)   | inkmap -- per-pixel foreground coverage for photographed marks.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
